reason: The memo's LRU capacity doubled to 1024 by the CONST operator; the memo it bounds is an exact cache, so the constant's value decides only which repeats are reused and how many keys are retained, never a number any check reads. A hit returns the (value, gradient) an earlier evaluation of the same x computed, to the bit (the wrapper's own contract; the batched answers it caches are asserted equal to scipy's per variable by tests/features.py::_grad_parity), so plans, costs and gradients are identical for any bound at or above the per-solve reuse span -- measured p99 = 111 evaluations in the constant's own comment. The bound is a memory cap, not a tuning constant: an x key is ~0.8 KiB, so 1024 entries stay near 1 MiB of retained state, orders of magnitude under the 27-41 MiB row-matrix key cost this memo replaced, and the stress gate's per-scenario traced peaks are bounded under either value.
